question: Will Trump demolish the Kennedy Center before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no demolition. The Sept 17 order requires 30 days' written notice before any demolition, and notice would set off an injunction fight. Trump said reconstruction won't begin until appeals courts rule on his name, and those appeals are pending. The center's spokesperson said 'nothing is being demolished.' Upside risk: the East Wing precedent, repeated threats, the 'Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED' placard, and DOJ calling the building unsound. The partial-demolition clause (more than de minimis) adds a little risk. Markets: Polymarket 'demolition announced by Dec 31' is about 0.34-0.47 on roughly $1k volume, but it measures an announcement, not destruction; Manifold 0.32 runs to 2029. Neither matches this question.

- May 2026: Judge Christopher Cooper (D.D.C., Beatty v. Trump 1:25-cv-04480) ruled only Congress can rename; preliminary injunction blocked the closure for the $257M renovation. DOJ appealed to the D.C. Circuit, and an appeals court declined to overrule the judge. Sept 15: Cooper again barred the Trump name wording; the Center appealed that ruling to the D.C. Circuit and DOJ plans to seek expedited review (CNBC/CNN Sept 15).
- Sept 15 (CNBC): Trump said renovation/reconstruction 'will not take place' unless an appeals court or the Supreme Court allows his name; the board voted to close the center for renovations.
- Sept 16-17 (NPR/CNN/CBS): Trump said the center 'will end up being ripped down' if he gets no credit; photographed with a 'Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED' placard on Air Force One. Center spokesperson Roma Daravi: 'nothing is being demolished.' Fencing went up around the building.
- Sept 17 (Axios/PBS): Cooper ordered 30 days' written notice before any change to the scope of renovations, 'including but not limited to any demolition' of the main building, and required a sworn status report on the closure.
- Sept 23 (WaPo/Forbes): Exec director Matt Floca's sworn declaration extends the closure through at least Sept 30, reevaluated weekly, citing 'widespread' deterioration and soffit corrosion (Walter P. Moore engineering report).
- Sept 26-27 (US News/The Hill): Former employees allege leadership halted planned repairs and diverted $9.3M in congressional funds to cosmetic work.
- Separate suit: historic preservation/architecture groups sued to block changes to the building (Yahoo/AOL).
- Precedent: the White House East Wing was demolished quickly without prior approval in the ballroom project (Oct 2025); the Kennedy Center differs because an explicit 30-day notice order is in place.
- Status quo: building closed and fenced, standing; no demolition notice filed as far as searches found.
- Resolves off actual intentional destruction of more than a de minimis portion of the structure, not off announcements or threats.
- Event window: question open (2026-09-28) -> before 2027-01-01; as of 2026-09-29 about 25% of the Jan-1-anchored quarter elapsed (~94 days remain). Any notice would need to be filed by about Dec 1 to allow demolition within the window.
- Searched but not found: any filed 30-day demolition notice, a demolition contract or permit, a D.C. Circuit decision date, or news after Sept 27.
